short: An English philosopher whose masterpiece Leviathan established the foundation for modern Western political philosophy and social contract theory.
full:
Thomas Hobbes was a prominent English philosopher best known for his foundational contributions to political philosophy. Writing against the backdrop of the bloody English Civil War, he developed a deeply pessimistic view of human nature. In his 1651 masterpiece *Leviathan*, Hobbes argued that humanity's natural state—without government or laws—is a "war of all against all," in which life is inevitably "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short."

To escape this state of nature, Hobbes proposed that individuals must enter into a social contract, surrendering their absolute freedoms to a strong, undivided central authority. Unlike later thinkers who argued for popular sovereignty, Hobbes believed that only an absolute sovereign—the Leviathan—could maintain order, prevent civil war, and provide the security necessary for society to function. Though his support for absolute monarchy alienated both Parliamentarians and Royalists of his day, his secular framework for state authority and his conception of the social contract reshaped Western political thought.
